abstract: A rare case of a colon carcinoma that developed in a 50-year-old woman is documented. Histologically, the removed tumor was composed of two distinctive elements, i.e., well-differentiated papillary adenocarcinoma and choriocarcinoma. It was strongly suggested that the latter malignancy derived from the pre-existing colonic carcinoma through metaplastic proliferation. A very high human chorionic gonadotropin level was noted in the patient's serum obtained at the preoperative stage. Autopsy materials revealed that metastatic foci in the liver, lungs, and lymph nodes were exclusively composed of choriocarcinoma.
abstract_ja: 50歳女性に発生した大腸癌の稀な症例を報告する。組織学的に、切除された腫瘍は高分化乳頭状腺癌と絨毛癌という2つの成分から成っていた。後者の悪性腫瘍は、既存の大腸癌から化生性増殖により生じたことが強く示唆された。術前の血清ヒト絨毛性ゴナドトロピン(hCG)値は非常に高かった。剖検では、肝、肺、リンパ節の転移巣が絨毛癌のみから成っていた。
